# title: "Resources"
title-block-banner: true
body-classes: usefullinks
---

A collection of tools, data sources, and learning materials I recommend to students and use in my own research. **Students starting out:** begin with the *Learn to Code* and *Economics Data* sections.

---

## Learn to Code

::: {.card-grid}

::: {.card}
### 🟣 Julia Academy

Free courses for programming, machine learning, and data science. Start here if you have never coded before.

🔗 [Link](https://juliaacademy.com/courses)
:::

::: {.card}
### 📘 QuantEcon

Open lectures on quantitative economics with Julia and Python — the single best bridge between economics and programming.

🔗 [Link](https://quantecon.org)
:::

::: {.card}
### 💻 Learn C++

Tutorials for when you need serious speed (structural models, large simulations).

🔗 [Link](https://www.learncpp.com)
:::

::: {.card}
### 📗 Coding for Economists

Arthur Turrell's free book: Python, data, and good practice — written for economists.

🔗 [Link](https://aeturrell.github.io/coding-for-economists/intro.html)
:::

::: {.card}
### 🧰 Code and Data for the Social Sciences

Gentzkow & Shapiro's classic guide to organising code and data so your project doesn't collapse.

🔗 [Link](https://www.brown.edu/Research/Shapiro/pdfs/CodeAndData.pdf)
:::

::: {.card}
### 🖥️ The Missing Semester

MIT's crash course in the computing skills nobody teaches: shell, git, editors.

🔗 [Link](https://missing.csail.mit.edu/)
:::

:::

---

## Economics Data

::: {.card-grid}

::: {.card}
### 🇺🇸 FRED

Federal Reserve Economic Data — the first stop for macro time series. Free, with API access.

🔗 [Link](https://fred.stlouisfed.org)
:::

::: {.card}
### 🇬🇧 ONS & Bank of England

UK official statistics and the Bank's interactive statistical database.

🔗 [ONS](https://www.ons.gov.uk) · [BoE Database](https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/boeapps/database/)
:::

::: {.card}
### 🌍 World Bank Open Data

Cross-country development and macro indicators.

🔗 [Link](https://data.worldbank.org)
:::

:::

---

## Math and Statistics Notes

::: {.card-grid}

::: {.card}
### 📊 Math & Probability Notes

Lecture materials and notes on probability theory.

🔗 [Link](https://math.dartmouth.edu/~prob/prob/prob.pdf)
:::

::: {.card}
### 📈 Bayesian Econometrics

Applied Bayesian Econometrics for Central Bankers — practical and code-driven.

🔗 [Link](https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/ccbs/applied-bayesian-econometrics-for-central-bankers-updated-2017)

## LaTeX & Writing

::: {.card-grid}

::: {.card}
### ✍️ Overleaf

Online LaTeX editor — what you will write your dissertation in.

🔗 [Link](https://www.overleaf.com)
:::

::: {.card}
### 📐 LaTeX Table Generator

Easy table builder for LaTeX.

🔗 [Link](https://www.tablesgenerator.com/latex_tables)
:::

::: {.card}
### ✏️ Hemingway Editor

Improve clarity and readability of writing.

🔗 [Link](https://hemingwayapp.com)
:::

::: {.card}
### 🤖 QuillBot

Paraphrasing and writing assistant.

🔗 [Link](https://quillbot.com)
:::

:::

## Writing Economics

Essential reading before you write a dissertation, thesis, or paper.

::: {.card-grid}

::: {.card}
### ✒️ Economical Writing

Deirdre McCloskey's principles of clear economics writing, in a short PDF.

🔗 [Link](https://www.deirdremccloskey.com/docs/pdf/Article_309.pdf)
:::

::: {.card}
### 📝 Writing Tips for PhD Students

John Cochrane's famous guide — blunt, practical, and just as useful for a dissertation.

🔗 [Link](https://static1.squarespace.com/static/5e6033a4ea02d801f37e15bb/t/5eda74919c44fa5f87452697/1591374993570/phd_paper_writing.pdf)
:::

::: {.card}
### 🎯 The Introduction Formula

Keith Head's recipe for the hardest part of any paper: the introduction.

🔗 [Link](http://blogs.ubc.ca/khead/research/research-advice/formula)
:::

::: {.card}
### 🪜 Four Steps to an Applied Micro Paper

Jesse Shapiro's systematic method for going from question to paper.

🔗 [Link](https://www.brown.edu/Research/Shapiro/pdfs/foursteps.pdf)
:::

:::

## Presenting Your Work

::: {.card-grid}

::: {.card}
### 🎤 Academic Presenting: How to Get It Right

David Ubilava's practical guide to presenting a paper.

🔗 [Link](https://davidubilava.com/misc/paper-presentation.html)
:::

::: {.card}
### 📊 Ten Guidelines for Better Tables

Jon Schwabish on turning unreadable tables into convincing ones.

🔗 [Link](https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/journal-of-benefit-cost-analysis/article/ten-guidelines-for-better-tables/74C6FD9FEB12038A52A95B9FBCA05A12)
:::

::: {.card}
### 📈 Data Visualization

Kieran Healy's free book on making figures that actually communicate.

🔗 [Link](https://socviz.co/)
:::

::: {.card}
### 🖼️ Best Figures in Economics

Paul Goldsmith-Pinkham's gallery of great figures — steal ideas from the best.

🔗 [Link](https://paulgp.github.io/best_figures.html)
:::

:::

## Doing Research

::: {.card-grid}

::: {.card}
### 🔍 An Unofficial Guide to Empirical Work

Amy Finkelstein on how empirical research actually gets done — false starts included.

🔗 [Link](http://wenxingxiang.weebly.com/uploads/6/0/5/1/60518841/an_unofficial_guide_to_trying_to_doempirical_work.pdf)
:::

::: {.card}
### 🔧 The Economist as Plumber

Esther Duflo on economics as practical problem-solving.

🔗 [Link](https://www.aeaweb.org/articles?id=10.1257/aer.p20171153)
:::

::: {.card}
### 🧭 Tips for Economists

Masayuki Kudamatsu's encyclopedic collection of advice for every stage.

🔗 [Link](https://sites.google.com/site/mkudamatsu/tips4economists)
:::

::: {.card}
### 🎓 Econ Grad Advice

Curated guidance if you are considering or starting a PhD in economics.

🔗 [Link](https://sites.google.com/view/econgradadvice/)
:::

:::
